findings.proposal: In quaySprayEmit/quayBuildSpray, cut the sheet size to about 0.35 times current, double the count within the same InstancedMesh (quaySPRAY_N 22 to 44), give each one a tumble (random axis spin) and a 0.6 s life with scale going to 0 in the last 40%. Change the colour to PALETTE.foam from the cream sail tone. Shrink the bow puff spheres to 0.5 times and lift them 0.4 m so they leave the hull as a plume. Draw calls stay the same.

findings.title: [quay] 'Earn a dolphin escort' is free: it ticks 11 s after taking the wheel
findings.evidence: Took the helm at t 40.8, and 'dolphin-escort' was done at t 52.4 with nothing but W held. The rule is 'hold better than 6.5 m/s for six seconds', which full throttle does by default. A task named 'earn' should be earned, and here it also uses up the harbour's best moment in the first 100 m.
findings.proposal: Only let the dolphins surface (quayDolphinOn) once the boat is past Bradleys Head (quayBoatZ < quayBRAD.z) and within 20 m of the rhumb line between the next buoy pair. The escort then becomes the reward for steering the open-harbour stretch well, it lands mid-passage, and the rest of the rule stays as it is.

findings.title: [manly] The arrival frame is the back of a blank billboard, a bin and zebra planks
findings.evidence: b0-manly-01-arrive.png, the first frame of 'the sea has a shape here': about 35% of the frame is dithered crossing planks, then the bin, then the blank cream back of a noticeboard. The ocean is a thin grey band on the horizon, and the break, the flags and the swell are not in shot.
findings.proposal: After fixing the bin, set the chapter's arrival lens to look down the beach over the break: the resting lens already described at (11.6, 6.7, 48.4). Alternatively, spawn at the top of the centre beach steps (x -12, z 38) facing -z, so the first thing on screen is a set breaking across the whole frame. Turn the noticeboard 180 degrees so its painted face (not the blank back) faces the promenade.

findings.title: [free-roam] The Free Roam picker shows the story grouping, not the 19 tiles the owner asked for
findings.evidence: b0-free-00.png: 'Free roam' opens 'Where would you like to start?' with a big Sydney hero card, a 'A little further' fold holding 2 tiles, and collapsed folds 'In good company' and 'Other people's rhythms', plus '2 MORE BELOW'. Only 3 of 19 places are visible. The owner explicitly asked for the 19 tiles in one clean grid for Free Roam.
findings.proposal: When the picker is opened from Free Roam, skip the hero and fold layout and render one 5x4 grid of all 19 painted tiles (the same tile art and key corners). Keep the story layout for Story Mode. No save change.

summary: I played all four chapters with real keys in session tr-biome1. The laptop was shared with other reviewers, so the governor sat at perfRung 3 the whole time (median frame 62-82 ms). That means reflections, far planes and full shadows were parked, and my beauty calls take that into account. What each place is works well. Pasto's plaza, with its bunting, a llama and a vendor chasing the animal, is lively. Cali's party bus is noisy and colourful, with a band on the roof. Copacabana's wave pavement, the kiosk and the Globo man read as Rio at a glance. In the Pantanal, the herd answers each call on a rising pitch and the cowbird rides the animal's back. What keeps the group from a 10 is that three of the four headline moments failed or got in each other's way when I played them for real. In Pasto the condor ended up on the paving next to the animal and was never grabbable (0 of 100 samples in reach). In Rio the fragata is called with the same Q, in the same 13 m circle, as the three-wheek travel door. In Cali an idle passenger fell off the party bus about 30 m into the ride and the bus drove on without it. The places also lose their sense of where they are at the edges: Pasto's horizon is grey pyramids rather than the Andean patchwork, and the Pantanal's mirror water turns to olive mud as soon as the governor steps down.

findings.title: [pasto] After the second whistle the condor settles on the plaza paving and can never be grabbed
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/tb3-pasto.js on a fresh file, standing at the plaza spawn (0,26): Q, wait 5 s, Q, then 10 s of sampling. condor.state was 'circling' for 100/100 samples, talonInReach() was true in 0/100, and the talon-to-animal distance got as low as 1.45 m. In other words the bird was standing on the ground beside the capybara. Screenshot qa/ten-review/tb3-pasto-02-plaza-low.png shows the black condor lying flat on the paving next to the animal, with the paper still saying 'Q again to bring it lower, then hold E under it'. In the earlier run (tb2-pasto-03-grab.png) E was held for 3 s and nothing happened (mounted:false). condorPickupReady() requires p.y - terrain > 4 and a launch path clear of scenery for 1.4 s, so a bird parked on the plaza can never pass. This was at rung 3, but weaker laptops sit there too, and this is the chapter's headline moment.
findings.proposal: In the low-orbit branch of the condor update, clamp the bird's target height to max(condorORBIT_LOW_Y + capy.y, condorGroundTop(x,z) + condorHANG + 3.5), so it can never reach the paving. Then add a watchdog: if condorLowered && !condorPickupReady() for 3 s in a row, move the orbit centre to the nearest open point (a ring search on condorGroundTop, 8 bearings x 8/14/20 m) and say 'it will not come down under the flags. somewhere with more sky.' through game.toast. Point the paper's where() for condor-ride at that point too. Add a harness row condorAudit().stuckT so the soak catches it. Gate the reposition behind game.state.noCondorOpen.

findings.title: [rio] The three-wheek travel door sits on the fragata summon spot, so calling the bird opens the travel board
findings.evidence: CHAPTERS puts Rio's marquee at Arpoador (-62,-26), and the fragata is called there with Q. atRio in systems.js:52799 is game.rio.inZone('arpoador'), which is rioARPOADOR r=13 (rio.js:53). The home counter at systems.js:52943 counts every input.whistlePressed inside that zone and calls boardOpen() on the third, and it only excludes the player while mounted. In tb2-rio-03-grab.png, after the call and the lower (two Qs), the pill 'wheek three times to go home ○○○' is sitting in the middle of the marquee frame. A player who presses Q a third time because the bird is slow to come down gets the travel board in the middle of the chapter's star moment.
findings.proposal: In homeOk, add && !(game.condor && game.condor.active) && !(game.state.flierWhistleT > 0), and have condorSummon() set game.state.flierWhistleT = 6 whenever it consumes a whistle (in the circling and inbound branches). Better still, move Rio's door off the rock to the Posto 6 fishermen's end or the kiosk line: add an inZone('posto6') box in rio.js and change the CHAPTERS 'way' line to match. The rock then belongs only to the bird and the applause. Pasto's crater door has the same shape (condor-ride and thermal-peak also use Q near the crater), so apply the same guard there.

findings.title: [cali] An idle passenger slides off the party bus about 30 m in, and the bus carries on without it
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/tb2-cali.js called game.cali.roofPlace(0) with the chiva parked and then gave no input. At 3 s chivaDebug() reported st:'rolling', onRoof:true, s=2.9, and the paper card showed 'THE BIG ONE · NOW, on the roof · 0 of 10 cables'. By 15 s the animal was at (-0.4, 0.7, 40.5) on the pavement with onRoof:false, wiresTouched 0 and hits 0. The chiva went on to s=177 with nobody on board (tb2-cali-03-ride.png, 05-ride3.png). No line told the player they had missed her. The paper just switched back to 'Ride the party bus roof up… 60 m'. This was at rung 3, where the world steps under a 1/20 s clock, which is exactly where a moving floor loses friction.
findings.proposal: Hold a passenger to the roof whenever there is no input. When caliOnRoof has been true within the last 0.3 s, the animal is inside the roof's local box plus 0.4 m, and no move key is held, snap its horizontal velocity to the chiva's frame velocity each substep (the same carry-frame write rio's bonde uses), so only a deliberate walk or a cable takes it off. Add a missed-her beat: if the animal leaves the roof while st is 'rolling' and no cable hit caused it, say 'she does not stop for anybody. she goes round again.' and show caliChivaNextIn on the paper, the same way nextIn works for Pasto's carroza. Flag: noChivaHold.

findings.title: [pasto] Whistling for the condor gives no camera beat, so the bird arrives out of shot
findings.evidence: condorSummon (condor.js:965-1063) spawns the bird 46 m out at a random bearing and 56 m up, then toasts 'something enormous turns overhead'. Nothing moves the camera. In tb2-pasto-02-called.png the locals are saying 'Look at the size of that thing.' while the frame shows level plaza, stalls and a bench, and no condor anywhere (it was at (-1.8,14.1,26.1), behind the lens). Rio's fragata uses the same module, so it has the same gap. The only framed shot in this file, condorShot, runs at the launch, after the player has already found the bird.
findings.proposal: On the first summon of each chapter visit, call game.frameShot({ yaw: atan2(bird.x - capy.x, bird.z - capy.z) + PI, dist: 11, pitch: -22*PI/180 (looking up), raise: 1.5, hold: 2.6 }) as soon as the bird crosses 30 m from the animal while inbound. That keeps the animal in the bottom third with the wings turning above it. Play the whistle's echo as a second, lower wheek 0.6 s later through game.sfx('whistle',{pitch:0.8,volume:0.5}) so the call sounds answered. Flag game.state.noSummonShot, which costs nothing when cut. It fixes Pasto and Rio in one place.

findings.title: [pasto] The horizon is 21 grey pyramids, not the Andean patchwork Nariño is known for
findings.evidence: Every Pasto frame I took (tb1-pasto-02-list, tb2-pasto-03-grab, tb1-pasto-06-wander) closes on sharp 4- and 5-sided grey cones 60-110 m tall. They come from pastoPEAK_RINGS (pasto.js:563-566) using ConeGeometry(1,1,4|5). Behind the plaza they read as generic low-poly mountains that could be any chapter's. The real view from Pasto, and Nariño's signature, is the colcha de retazos: rounded green ridges quilted with fields in greens and ochres, with hedgerows between them.
findings.proposal: Keep the far ring (r 184, pale andesFog) as the one silhouette of volcanoes. Replace the near ring with a closed ridge strip: one BufferGeometry annulus from r 140 to 175, 96 x 6 quads, with a smooth sum-of-sines profile rising 18-45 m. Give each quad a vertex colour picked from 5 existing PALETTE field tones (grass greens, andesSun ochre, a ploughed brown) on a 2 x 3 quad patch grid, and darken the quad edges along the patch borders as hedgerows (PALETTE.peakFar). Flat Lambert, one draw call, about 1.2k tris, no shadows. The patchwork must show from the plaza (y about 4) and from condor altitude. The ring is static, so it needs no flag. It lays over the existing layout and re-bases nothing.

findings.title: [rio] Arpoador's boulders are drawn but not solid, right where the marquee happens
findings.evidence: rioBuildArpoador (rio.js:1660-1680) scatters 22 boulders at random with up to 3 m radius (M.sph) across the rock and never adds a collider (no rioStaticBox). When I placed the animal on the rock (tb2-rio-01b/03-grab.png) it stood inside a boulder. The rock showed a dithered hole with the animal's colour showing through, and it then sank to y -0.9 in the surf. The call, the applause crowd and the marquee framing all happen on this rock, so a player walks through its stones while trying to get under the bird.
findings.proposal: For each sphere with s > 1.4, add a rioStaticBox that fits the drawn half-extents (s, s*0.55, s) at the same x/z and yaw 0, pooled into one body the way pastoBody pools the bunting posts. Also swap rand() for a seeded rioRnd so the rock is the same on every visit, which the collider needs anyway. A differential with qa/audit-solid2.js (walk at each stone) proves it.

findings.title: [pantanal] Arrival hitches for about a second, and it is the only chapter in my group that does
findings.evidence: The same 3 s rAF sample right after the arrival fade, on the same loaded machine: Pasto p95 120 ms, Cali 67.8, Rio 69.0, Pantanal p95 900 ms with a max of 1199 ms, only 22 frames in 3 s (qa/tb1-pantanal.json.png). The first frame (tb1-pantanal-01-arrival.png) is still under the white wash at t=14.8 s. A spike this size on top of a steady 66 ms median points to first-use shader compiles, most likely the flood's grainOwn water with the reflection, the dusk-tinted sheet and the lily and firefly materials, landing in the first visible frames. HANDOFF records the same shape for Palawan's manta (fixed by warming during the fade).
findings.proposal: In the Pantanal onEnter, while the white card is still up, call renderer.compile(scene, camera) once with the chapter root and the dormant dusk, firefly and jaguar groups set visible for that single call, then restore their visibility. This is the Palawan manta pattern. Measure it with qa/aaa-ab.mjs-style GPU timers on a fresh profile: arrival p95 over the first 3 s should drop to within about 1.5x the chapter's steady frame time. Flag: noPanWarm.

findings.title: [pantanal] At any governor rung above 0 the mirror flood turns to olive mud
findings.evidence: The water is meant to be 'a MIRROR: what you see is not the water, it is the sky in the water' (pantanal.js:3568). The planar reflection (reflect k 1.0, pantanal.js:611) parks at rung >= 1. In every play shot (tb1-pantanal-03-midway, tb2-pantanal-03-midriver) the flood is flat opaque khaki, the lily pads float on what looks like mud, and the caimans read as flat black wedges. Players on laptops that step down lose the chapter's defining picture.
findings.proposal: Add a cheap fallback inside grain() for this material, used only when the reflection is parked. Take the view-space Fresnel you already compute (fresnel 0.65) and mix toward a two-stop vertical sky gradient (PALETTE panSky, a lightened panHaze) instead of toward the sheet colour, so grazing angles show pale sky. Then subtract a soft dark band where the gallery-forest silhouette would reflect, as a function of view direction only (a sin band on atan2(view.x, view.z) scaled by the tree line), for the look of reflected trees. That is roughly 0.03 ms. Flag noPanSkyFresnel, active only while perfRung >= 1. Check it with a hide-and-diff mask on the water at rung 1.

findings.title: [cali] The lens fade clears only a 0.7 m band of a lamp post, so the pole still splits the frame
findings.evidence: In tb1-cali-04-marquee.png a black utility pole stands between the camera and the animal. Only a band of it at chest height is dithered (sysLENS_CAP_R = 0.7 m capsule, systems.js:643). The rest of the pole stays a solid black bar through the middle of the screen. The Pantanal version is worse: in tb1-pantanal-06-wander.png the capsule fade on a bush shows as a hard-edged rectangular screen-door slab across a third of the frame, with the animal cut off at the bottom edge.
findings.proposal: When the capsule test hits a mesh flagged userData.thin (poles, lamp posts, trunks; set in caliBuildWires and panBuild*), fade the whole mesh through the existing vLensFade per-draw uniform instead of the capsule, and bias the boom by sysLENS_OUT for as long as the hit lasts. For foliage clumps, taper the capsule's fade edge over 0.5 m (smoothstep on distance to the capsule axis) so the fade has a soft radial edge rather than a rectangle. This is the existing noLensCap A/B, with one new flag noLensThin.

findings.title: [pasto] The arrival lens looks up into the drizzle, so the first frame is mostly brown sticks
findings.evidence: tb1-pasto-01-arrival.png is the chapter's first picture. The arrival lens pitches up at Galeras from under the bunting, and the frame is full of long dark diagonal streaks and grey chips. That is the 'Andean Drizzle' rain field (weather.js:282, rain odds 0.46) drawn as BoxGeometry streaks inside a 10 m box around the camera (weather.js:936, wxRAIN_BOX_R 588), plus the motes. Seen from below against the sky, the streaks read as twigs falling around the volcano, not rain, and they bury the plume and the cone.
findings.proposal: Two changes, both laid over the existing rows with nothing re-based. (1) A rain start delay: in wxPrime(to), when the arrival lens is up (game.state.arriveLens or the first 20 s after a cross), hold rainWant at 0 so the first frame of every chapter is dry and the shower rolls in later. The weather row stays the same. (2) A streak term that depends on pitch: scale each streak's length by (1 - 0.7*max(0, camPitchUp)) and lerp its colour toward the sky fog colour as the camera pitches up, so rain seen against the sky reads pale and short. Flag noRainPitch, which costs nothing when cut.

findings.title: [pantanal] Gathering the herd takes nine separate wheeks, one recruit each
findings.evidence: herdToCrossing() placed the nine capybaras beside the animal. One Q recruited exactly one (herdAudit: 1 row 'follow', 8 'graze'). After a 14 s swim toward the river the other eight were still grazing at the start (tb2-pantanal-03-midriver). The recruit loop (pantanal.js:4047-4061) takes the single nearest non-follower per wheek. The rising answer figure is lovely, but it has to be pressed out nine times, and the crossing clue asks for 4 before you can start. The chapter is about 'the world falls in behind you', and in play it feels like clicking.
findings.proposal: Make the herd cascade: after the third recruit, each further wheek recruits the nearest one plus any grazer within 5 m of a follower, capped at 3 per wheek. Their answers keep the rising scale, each 0.12 s after the last. Wheeking with 5+ followers makes the remaining grazers within 16 m look up (the look=1 path) and trail after the line at graze speed for 6 s. The chorus arrives sooner and the crossing starts after 3-4 wheeks instead of 9. No save field is involved, since following is live state. Flag noHerdCascade.

findings.title: [rio] The Copacabana frontage sits in deep shade, so half the beach frame is grey slabs
findings.evidence: In tb1-rio-06-wander.png, looking along the beach, the left half of the frame is apartment blocks in heavy shade: dark grey, near-black windows, palms against a dark wall. The right half is bright sand and sea. The Avenida Atlântica is famously a bright wall of white and pastel buildings, and here it reads as a gloomy concrete canyon. The blocks use rioWall1/2/3/5 (rio.js:2320-2400). The seaward faces are shaded because of where the sun sits, and that sun must not be re-based.
findings.proposal: Leave the sun alone and lay a bounce term over it. The frontage faces a 100 m-wide bright beach, so add a sand-bounce vertex colour to the seaward faces in rioBuildFrontage: lerp each face's colour 25% toward PALETTE.rioPavePale, weighted by the face's normal dot the -z (sea) direction and fading with height (strongest on the bottom two floors). Scatter lit window rows (PALETTE warm window colour) on 1 in 6 windows so the wall has life when it goes to dusk. It is baked, so it costs nothing per frame. Flag noRioBounce, checked by a hide-and-diff mask on the frontage band.

findings.title: [cali] Chiva cables are drawn as thick black bars across the spawn street
findings.evidence: In tb1-cali-02-list.png, taken at the spawn, five or six black cables cross the upper-left third of the frame as heavy bars, thicker than the palm trunks, running into the camera. caliBuildWires (cali.js:2079-2110) builds them as catenaries at caliWIRE_Y 4.2 m plus 1.42 m, which puts them at the follow camera's eye height for most of the town, and they are what frames the first impression of Cali. They are a real hazard on the chiva route, but at the spawn they only add clutter.
findings.proposal: Draw the cables at about half their current radius, in a mid-grey from PALETTE (a dark metal, not black), and fade any cable segment within 5 m of the camera through the existing vLensFade uniform. That keeps the wires readable from the roof, where they are the challenge, and clears them from the walking camera. Flag noWireFade.

area: biome group 4: sahara (ch8 Marrakech), venice (ch10), goreme (ch13 Cappadocia), monaco (ch18)
summary: I played each chapter with real keys at a fresh save, 2 to 3 runs each, and went back for the Sahara jetpack, the Cappadocia balloon and the Monaco car. The best frames are really good: the dune crest looking back at the Koutoubia and the palmeraie, the St Mark's facade and clock tower, pre-dawn Cappadocia under the balloons, and the Monaco grid at night in front of the stand. Two of the four marquees are broken right now. In Monaco the animal is not in the red car it is driving (measured 8.7 m apart while atHelm is true). In Cappadocia the chase truck parks its trailer collider on the launch basket, and in two runs the animal could not board. Beyond the bugs, three camera problems keep it off a 10. Venice has no camera ceiling under the Procuratie arcades. The Monaco race camera gets buried behind terrain. The jetpack paper keeps showing an unrelated task while the jetpack run is on, so the player flies off the course into a void. On beauty, the Sahara day sky blends into the sand as one khaki colour, Monaco's harbour boats look like pontoons, and the Marrakech arrival is a tiled floor plus a 275 m walk over an empty plain. The small mischief (orange cart, snake basket, spritz, pigeons) ticks within 15 to 20 s of arrival and feels good. Headless timing was about 15 fps at perfRung 3 in every chapter.

findings.title: [monaco] BUG: the capybara is not in the red car it is driving
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/tr4m-monaco.js: I pressed E at the car and held W. The car drove the circuit at 20-30 m/s. qa/ten-review/tr4-car.js measured capy.atHelm=true with the capy at (153.9,10.2,0.9) and the monMeCar mesh at (150.2,8.5,-7), 8.7 m apart. In tr4-car-now.png the animal is standing on the road behind the red car under the bridge. In tr4m-monaco-04-drive.png it is on the hillside about 5 m to one side of the car. Likely cause: the seat is written from the analytic target (monMeTX/TY/TZ) but the car mesh is copied from monMeBody.interpolatedPosition. monMePlace(dt) only sets a velocity on that body, and main.js caps the physics at 2 substeps once perfRung >= MAIN_SHED_RUNG. At low frame rates the body only covers part of each frame's travel, so the car falls further behind the target (and the seat) every frame.
findings.proposal: Use one pose for both. In monMePlace(dt>0), also do b.position.set(tx,ty,tz) (keep the velocity for contacts), and in the race update draw monMeG at (monMeTX, monMeTY, monMeTZ) with the yaw from monMeYaw instead of from interpolatedPosition/Quaternion. Do the same to the pack cars if they use the same pattern. Test: probe |capy - monMeCar| < 1 m over a whole lap at perfRung 0 and 3, and take a picture of the capy on the roof or in the seat.

findings.title: [goreme] BUG: the chase truck parks its trailer on the launch basket and blocks boarding
findings.evidence: In two separate runs (tr4-goreme.js, then tr4m-goreme.js with 40 s of steering plus hops) the animal stopped 2.19-2.26 m from the basket at (-0.66,4.54,0.17) and never got aboard, so 'aboard' and 'sunrise' could not start. tr4-near.js listed the physics bodies there: basket body 250 at (0,4.32,-2) and the trailer bed KINEMATIC body 248 at (0.5,5.05,-1.7) with 1.3x0.12x2.1 half-extents and side rails, i.e. the bed overlaps the basket. tr4m-goreme-03-aboard.png shows the capy wedged between the green truck and a poplar trunk, with the basket behind. gorUpdateTruck chases gorBalX/Z + wind*fall even while the balloon is on the ground (fall = 0), so the truck drives from (20,10) onto the pad and stops at d<3, which puts the trailer 2.4 m behind it, right on the basket.
findings.proposal: In gorUpdateTruck, hold the truck at its parking spot (20,10, yaw 0) until the balloon is airborne (gorBalY - ground > 2) or a flight has started. When it chases a balloon that is landing, clamp its aim point to at least 7 m from (gorBalX,gorBalZ) so the trailer can never land on the basket collider. Test: from a fresh save, walk to hintTarget('aboard'), hop, and assert gorAboard within 10 s.

findings.title: [venice] The camera goes into the Procuratie arcades: dark wall frames and a dithered animal
findings.evidence: 2 of the 6 play shots were unusable. tr4-venice-03-spritz-theft.png (the spritz cafe under the arcade): the lens is inside the colonnade, the frame is 80% dark brown ceiling and pillar, the capy is a dithered close-up. tr4-venice-07-wander.png at (-17.9,1.3,-35.2): the camera is wedged between arcade piers with large yellow bokeh discs. Venice has no camCeil hook. Sahara solved the same problem for the souk with sahCamCeil (sahara.js:694), which it passes to the rig as camCeil and systems.js:50976 reads.
findings.proposal: Add venCamCeil(x,z) that returns the arcade soffit height (about 4.2 m) inside the footprints of both Procuratie colonnades and the cafe portico (the rectangles already built in venBuildSquares), and null elsewhere. Pass it as camCeil in the rig api, as Sahara does. Test: stand at (-17.4,0.9,-18.4) and (-17.9,1.3,-35.2), confirm the camera y stays below the soffit, and check by eye that the capy is not dithered.

findings.title: [sahara] The jetpack run: the paper shows the orange cart, so a free flight ends in a khaki void
findings.evidence: tr4m-sahara.js: strapped on at the crest (275,37,55), then held W+Space in 2.5 s bursts. The animal flew 130 m north to (263,14,173) and then west to (32,1,165), never passing a ring. In tr4m-sahara-05-flying.png the paper tab title reads 'Rob the orange juice cart 99+ m' with only a small subline 'to the minaret in 10.7 s'. No ring is on screen, and the sand and sky are the same khaki with no horizon. The wowLive line is shown, but the tab's head and arrow still point at the next unticked paper row.
findings.proposal: While wowLive is fresh (sysWOW_LIVE_STALE), switch the paper tab's title and arrow to the live marquee. Point the arrow at the next ring, from a new sahara hook game.wowTarget() -> {x,y,z} of sahJET_RINGS[sahJetNext] (or the minaret), and do the same for the Monaco lap and the Venice flood. Also give each ring a thin vertical PALETTE beam to the sand (flag noSahRingBeam, parked at rung >= 1) so it can be seen from 150 m.

findings.title: [sahara] The day sky is khaki, so sky and sand merge (the chapter looks smoggy)
findings.evidence: Every Sahara day shot (tr4-sahara-01, -03, -06, tr4m-sahara-05) has an olive-khaki sky close in value to the plaster and dune. From the air (tr4m-sahara-05-flying.png) there is no horizon at all. Cause: the sky colour is sahSkyDay lerped 0.62 toward sahSkyHot 0xd9d4bc ('nearly white'), and the haze sahHaze 0xe4cfa8 sits on top. The sky reads overcast in a chapter whose line is 'Forty-one degrees in the shade'.
findings.proposal: Leave the grade and fog as they are and add a zenith band over the dome: the top 35% of the sky lerps toward a new PALETTE.sahZenith (a saturated blue near 0x4f8fc4) by elevation, and the horizon stays hot and pale. That gives the 'white horizon, blue overhead' look and puts a value break behind the minaret and dune crests. Gate it with game.state.noSahZenith, park it at rung >= 1, fade it with the storm/dusk scalar the chapter already exports (sahara.js:6260) so the sandstorm still eats it, and check with the qa/aaa-ab.mjs A/B.

findings.title: [monaco] The race camera is buried behind terrain and the car barely shows
findings.evidence: tr4m-monaco-04-drive.png on the climb out of the harbour: 60% of the frame is a dark hillside and the red car is a small shape in the upper middle. tr4m-monaco-05-drive2.png: the lens is off the road among barriers and billboard slabs. At the start line (tr4-monaco-07-wander.png) the grid-and-stand composition is excellent, so the problem is the follow camera on the climbing, cut road.
findings.proposal: While monRaceOn, give the rig a race frame: a higher eye (+1.5 m), a shorter follow distance, and a look-ahead aim 12 m down the track from monTrackAt(monMeS+12), plus a camFloor that returns monRoad height + 2.5 on the circuit so the lens cannot sink into the cut banks. Use the same optional-hook shape as camFloor/camCeil (systems.js:30139).

findings.title: [sahara] The walk to the marquee is 275 m of empty flat plain
findings.evidence: The marquee is at (275,55) and the spawn at (0,8). The bot covered 40 m in 35 s. tr4-sahara-06-jetpack.png and -07-wander.png outside the walls: a uniform orange plane, sparse clusters of brown stakes, and a checker-stippled wall shadow. The camel ride exists ('Leave town on somebody's camel', caravan at 107,22), but nothing in the frame at the gate says so, and a walker gets nothing along the way.
findings.proposal: Dress the stretch from the gate to the palmeraie as a route people use, not a plane. Put a line of 8-10 telegraph poles along the staked track, fresh tyre ruts (the ground decal pass), and a donkey cart heading out on the same polyline as the caravan. At the gate, have a camel boy whose bubble says the caravan leaves 'when it leaves' and who kneels his camel when the animal comes within 6 m. That makes the ride the obvious answer, and the walk becomes optional. All of it uses existing instanced props and the caravan code.

findings.title: [monaco] The harbour boats read as pontoons, not the superyachts the place is famous for
findings.evidence: tr4-monaco-04-palace-guard.png (swimming in the port) and -03: the moored boats are flat white slabs with brown decks and one cube cabin plus a mast, the same height as the pontoons. From the water nothing says 'Monaco harbour'. The one real yacht (monBuildYacht) is the task boat; the rows at the quay are what fill the frame.
findings.proposal: Change the moored boats in monBuildHarbour so every third one is a 3-tier motor yacht: a stepped superstructure (3 boxes, each 70% of the one below), a dark window band in a PALETTE navy, a raked bow wedge and a thin pale hull stripe, merged into the existing instanced batch so it adds no draw calls. Add a lit window row on the top tier using the existing EMIT_OVER emitter pattern (monaco.js:2783) so they glow at night.

findings.title: [sahara] Four speech bubbles at once cover the best view in the chapter
findings.evidence: tr4m-sahara-03-crest.png: from the dune crest, the view back to the Koutoubia and the palmeraie (the chapter's best composition) is covered by four bubbles at once: 'The storytellers start at dusk...', 'Dust off the Atlas...', 'Chergui. Shut the shutters.', 'Walk up on the hard track...'. The Jemaa arrival (tr4-sahara-04) had two more on top of the ticked toast. The bubble pool is eight elements and nothing caps how many show at once (systems.js ~30772 only removes duplicate text).
findings.proposal: Cap visible NPC bubbles at 2. Priority goes to the nearest speaker and to any line addressed to the animal. Other bubbles queue for 2.5 s or fall back to the one-line heard pill. Also, bubbles from speakers more than 25 m away should use the heard pill, not a floating bubble.

findings.title: [sahara] The Jemaa el-Fnaa floor reads as a tiled kitchen floor, and the square has no evening smoke
findings.evidence: tr4-sahara-01-arrival.png and -02: the square is a terracotta grid of 6 m tiles with thick dark-red joints running to the horizon. That is the loudest pattern in the frame, and the real square is open, dusty, trodden plaster. There are no smoke columns over the food stalls, which are the square's signature from any distance.
findings.proposal: Cut the joint colour contrast by about 70% and break the lattice with 3-4 worn diagonal footpaths (a lighter PALETTE value) between the stalls, cart and snake basket, in sahBuildSquare. Add a slow grey-white smoke plume above each food stall from the existing weather mote pool (flag noSahStallSmoke, parked at rung >= 1). That puts a landmark over the stall rows you can see from the dune crest.

findings.title: [venice] The arrival frame is half blocked by a grey plinth and a traffic cone
findings.evidence: tr4-venice-01-arrival.png at the spawn (-4,13): St Mark's gilded domes are framed between the two Molo columns, which is good, but a large grey block (a plinth or utility box) fills the lower-left third right in front of the animal, and an orange traffic cone sits beside the right column. The first image of Venice is mostly slab.
findings.proposal: Nudge the spawn about 2.5 m east or yaw the arrival lens about 12 degrees right so the plinth moves out of the lower-left third, and move the cone to the passerelle stack where it tells the story. Pin the camera and check the before/after with the resting-lens probe (the resting lens is not deterministic between arrivals).

findings.title: [goreme] The dovecote approach is plain white boxes on flat grey ground
findings.evidence: tr4-goreme-05-dovecote.png at (-46,-2.6,-36.7): a zig-zag of five untinted white boxes (steps or blocks) crosses a flat, even grey slope dotted with dark holes. It looks like blockout, next to the carefully finished balloon field. The line that fires there ('eight hundred years of pigeons, and you are what happened to them.') is lovely, but nothing in the picture looks like tuff.
findings.proposal: Tint the treads with the valley's tuff PALETTE ramp (warm cream to rose), round their top edges with the existing round-on twin helper, and stagger their widths. Give the slope 2-3 painted dovecote bands (the white-ringed holes Cappadocia is known for) as flat decals on the cliff face over the dark holes, in gorBuildCliff's merger, so no draw calls are added.

findings.title: [goreme] The poplars glow chartreuse at pre-dawn and pull the eye off the balloons
findings.evidence: tr4-goreme-07-wander.png and -05: the conical poplars are the most saturated, brightest object in a blue-violet pre-dawn frame, brighter than the balloon envelopes that are supposed to be the subject. Next to the pale mare herd they read as neon.
findings.proposal: Tie the poplar instance colour to the dawn line (gorUpdateDawnLine already has the 0..1 of the sunrise). Start them at a desaturated olive and let them warm to their current yellow-green only as the sun clears the rim, so the valley 'lights up' with the marquee. Two PALETTE entries and one lerp, with a flag.

findings.title: [monaco] The promenade reads as dirt with red confetti, not pale Monaco stone
findings.evidence: tr4-monaco-03-pass-the-door.png on the harbour promenade: the ground is an even brown-grey with scattered small red squares, like litter. The lit facades and palms above it are strong, but the floor makes the richest town in the game look like a car park.
findings.proposal: Give the quay-side promenade a pale limestone PALETTE value with a 2 m paving lattice (the same joint trick as the Venice paving, at low contrast), and replace the red squares with a line of planters and bollards along the quay edge. That puts a clean pale band between the dark water and the lit facades.

area: biome group 3: iceland (ch7), antarctic (ch17), cave (ch16 Son Doong), drift (ch9)
summary: I played all four chapters in playwright session tr-biome3 on a fresh profile. I walked routes with real keys, used teleport-assisted runs for each marquee, took about 40 screenshots and got no console errors or lastError. The ideas are the best in the game: sitting in a hot pool until the sky answers, a cave you light with your own voice, a floating archipelago you jump through, and an orange tender running with orcas. Each place also has at least one screen that looks lovely: lit Reykjavik windows, the drift updraft shaft, the doline forest from above. What holds the group back is the same pattern in every chapter. The payoff moment is drawn with the cheapest primitives or gets covered up. The aurora is hard-edged green rectangles. Iceland's steam is grey octagon cards that fill the lens at the pool. The orcas are black crates. The drift cloud sea you land on after every fall reads as paving stones. On top of that, toasts, the expanded paper and NPC bubbles land on the marquee frame. There are also two real clarity bugs: the cave's first hint arrow sends you to a spot where the taught move does nothing, and the orca pod patrols through pack ice where the run cannot start.

findings.title: [antarctic] Orca marquee can stall for good: the pod patrols through 0.4-0.9 pack, where the boat can't reach the 4 m/s the run needs
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-antarctic.js: a closed-loop helm run with W held for 150 s, calling Q whenever the pod was within 180 m. Second escort formed near z=-440. withPod() then read 0.95-0.997 for over 45 s while boat speed sank to 2.8-3.3 m/s with the throttle full. The pod never broke into 'run', and orca-ride never ticked (log in qa/tr-biome3-mq-antarctic.json.png). Probe of packAt(): for z<-270 the east half of the patrol loop (x=20..60) reads 0.41-0.93. Patrol is px=8+42 sin(a), pz=-300+132 cos(a), so it spends about half its loop in heavy pack. The escort-to-run gate needs sp>4.0 (antarctic.js:4527), and nothing tells the player why the pod just sits there. The earlier 'run' had also dropped the pod back to patrol at (8,-432): the pod was 48 m away at t=20 s and 313 m away at t=25 s.
findings.proposal: Make the patrol follow the clear lead instead of an ellipse through the pack: in antUpdatePod patrol, set px = antLeadX(pz) + 10*sin(a*2), keeping pz = -300+132*cos(a). The pod then only ever forms up in water where 12.6 m/s is possible. As a belt-and-braces fix, scale the run gate by antBoatIce, e.g. sp > 4.0*(1-0.6*antBoatIce). Also add a one-shot toast when escort has lasted more than RUN_AT+4 s with sp<4, e.g. 'they want open water. find the lead.' No new save field; gate it behind a noPodLead flag for A/B.

findings.title: [iceland] The aurora is six hard-edged flat rectangles with no fall-off; the chapter's wow reads as green glass panes
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-iceland-03-aurora-rise.png and -05-aurora-look.png: at ignition the sky shows solid mint-green quads with a straight top and bottom edge and even brightness across the whole face, crossing behind the church. iceBuildAurora uses PlaneGeometry(len,h,40,1) with a single emissive colour per band. There is no vertical gradient and no alpha ramp, and a Lambert emissive ignores vertex colour, so there is no bright lower hem fading to nothing at the top like the real thing.
findings.proposal: Rebuild each band as PlaneGeometry(len, h, 40, 4) with a per-vertex colour attribute: row 0 (the hem) at 1.0 of PALETTE.iceAurora*, row 1 at 0.7, row 2 at 0.3, row 4 at 0. Pair it with MeshBasicMaterial({vertexColors:true, blending:Additive, depthWrite:false, fog:false}); under additive blending black is transparent, so the top dissolves and the hem glows. Tint the upper rows of band 1 toward iceAuroraMag for the violet crown, and taper both ends along x with the same ramp so no curtain has a vertical cut edge. Keep the per-vertex wave in iceUpdateAurora; it already moves x/y. Gate it as noAuroraRamp, parked at rung >= 2 by using 2 rows. Cost is the same draw count.

findings.title: [iceland] The aurora tick has no shot: the camera stays at pool level, the paper expands and NPC bubbles cover the sky
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-iceland-04-aurora-call.png, 3 s after the first successful call (aurora ticked). The camera is at the water looking horizontally at the pool rim. The curtains are only a glow at the top edge of the frame. The left third is covered by the expanded paper (part 1 of 3, four unticked Reykjavik tasks), and a local's bubble 'You are in a hot spring. What could you possibly need?' sits across the middle of the sky. iceAuroraCall only calls game.frameShot on iceAurRun % iceBURST_N === 0, the fourth in-time call (iceland.js:4566). The call that ticks the marquee gets no framing.
findings.proposal: On the first call that ticks 'aurora' (and on ignition, if the player is soaking), fire game.frameShot({ yaw: <bearing to the nearest curtain>+PI, pitch: -14deg (looking up), dist: 9, raise: 0.8, hold: 5 }). This puts the animal in the bottom third and the curtains in the top two thirds. For those 5 s, suppress the paper's tick expansion and NPC 'say' bubbles (wowLiveOn is already set; route barks through the existing sysPlaceLine path). Flag it noAuroraFrame.

findings.title: [iceland] Steam puffs are flat grey octagon cards that fill the frame at the pool and Strokkur, and the aurora burst spawns 14 of them in front of the lens
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-iceland-05-aurora-look.png and -07-geysir.png: a dozen large pale octagons with hard silhouettes cover the capybara and half the screen. iceBuildSteam uses SphereGeometry(0.5,5,4) at a constant opacity of 0.26 for the puff's whole life. iceSteamSync only grows the scale, so a puff reaches maximum size and then vanishes in one frame. iceAuroraCall's burst spawns 14 puffs within 3 m of the spring centre (iceland.js:4574-4577), which is exactly where the soaking animal and the camera are.
findings.proposal: (1) In iceSteamSync, shrink over the last 0.8 s of life, s *= smoothstep(0, 0.8, life), so puffs dissolve instead of popping. (2) Cull any puff within 4 m of game.camera.position by setting its scale to 0 in iceSteamSync. This costs one distance check per instance, 54 per frame. (3) Move the burst ring out to r=6-9 m on the far side of the spring from the camera, so it frames the animal rather than covering it. (4) Raise geometry detail to SphereGeometry(0.5,7,5) so the silhouette is not an octagon at close range. Flag it noSteamSoft.

findings.title: [cave] The first hint arrow sends the player into daylight, where the taught Q does nothing
findings.evidence: b3-cave run: I walked to the 'first-echo' hint target (0,46), whose paper line reads 'Q. in the dark. that is it.' and whose arrow shows 'here'. I pressed Q about 20 times over 15 s at 2.3 m from it and first-echo never ticked (qa/ten-review/b3-cave-03-first-echo.png shows the echo ring firing over green-lit grass). A later run pressed Q once at (-2,30) and it ticked immediately (b3m-cave-04-echo-05.png). cavWheek only ticks when cavDaylightAt < 0.25, which is smooth((z-30)/22), so z must be below about 34. The hint points at game.cave.mouth, about 12 m too far out, and the failure gives no feedback. It is the chapter's first lesson.
findings.proposal: Point the 'first-echo' where() at {x:0, z:cavMOUTH_Z-22} (z=28), the first spot that is actually dark. In cavWheek, when cavDaylightAt >= 0.25 and !cavToldEcho, show a one-shot toast: 'too much daylight here for it to come back. further in.' This is 3 lines plus 1 line of copy through the pools. No new save field.

findings.title: [all] Held toasts drain into the marquee: a stale cave lesson sits over the Drop into the Light
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-cave-07-col-fall.png: mid-fall off the column, with the signpost reading 'THE BIG ONE · NOW / FALLING · 5 m · 0 of 3 hoops'. The centre band of the screen shows the first-echo toast 'it comes back. that is how you see in here.', fired about 8 s earlier in the passage, right across the capybara. toast() only routes 'say' lines to the placed line when wowLiveOn at enqueue time (systems.js:30581). Lines parked in sysToastHeld by the freshness budget (30582-30588) are released later without re-checking wowLiveOn, so a stale line lands on the one frame the chapter is built around. The same clutter shows up in Iceland (bubble plus toast over the aurora) and in the drift (the puff tutorial toast at the first mid-air wheek).
findings.proposal: Where sysToastHeld is drained (the release path after sysFRESH_GAP), skip or keep holding any entry while wowLiveOn is true or a frameShot hold is active, and drop entries whose bio no longer matches the current biome or that are more than 12 s old. It is a single guard in the drain loop. Flag it noHeldWow.

findings.title: [antarctic] The orcas are box stacks and read as floating black crates from the chase camera
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-antarctic-03-pod-with.png and -04-end.png: the escort is four or five black rectangular clumps around the boat with square dorsal planks. No white flank or eye patch reads, because the white boxes sit low on the body (-0.52*s) and the camera is above and behind. antBuildPod makes the body from five M.box slabs plus a sphere head, the dorsal from one M.box, and the flukes from a flat box. The AAA pass rounded the other animals; this one was missed, and it is the star of chapter 17.
findings.proposal: Body: replace the five boxes with three overlapping stretched M.sph lobes (head, torso, tail stock) with smooth normals, per the 'what breathes' law, in PALETTE.antOrca. Dorsal: a 3-sided M.cone flattened to 0.18 wide, swept back 0.35 rad (bull straight, 2.1 m). Raise the eye patch to y=+0.34*s and scale it to 0.34 so it reads from 30 degrees of pitch. Add a thin antOrcaW belly crescent visible at the waterline. On each surfacing (the porpoise phase peak), spawn 6 white game.sparks at the blowhole. It is the same merger, so there is no draw-call change.

findings.title: [drift] The cloud sea you land on after every fall looks like hexagonal paving
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3-drift-06-updraft.png and -07-wander.png, and the landing in b3-drift-04-cloud-dive.png: the cloud floor is a field of flat-shaded lavender hexagons with dark facet edges, like cobbles or stones. The chapter header promises a 'slow lovely twelve seconds through the dark and a soft landing in cloud'. driBuildCloud's lobes are 228 squashed spheres through driMerger/driVC(), which is flat Lambert, at a low segment count, so each squashed sphere shows its 6-8 facets as a hard polygon. The landing view is a flat purple sheet with no depth (04-cloud-dive).
findings.proposal: Build the lobe merger with smooth normals (computeVertexNormals on the built geometry, flatShading false). A cloud is a volume, so it qualifies under the 'what breathes' exception. Raise each lobe to 10x6 segments. Give the top lobe of each mass a faint emissive of PALETTE.driCloudLit at 0.12 so tops go lighter than the sheet, as the comment intends. Add 12 low wisp sheets from driBuildWisps at y=2-6 over the sea, so a landing has something passing the lens. Flag it noCloudSoft; at rung >= 1 keep the smooth normals and drop the wisps.

findings.title: [cave] The echo, the chapter's torch, is a thin cyan arc and barely lights the cave
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-cave-05-echo-14.png, 1.4 s after a wheek in the dark passage: the only visible sign is a thin pale-blue arc about 3 px thick in the middle distance. The walls and roof stay near-black, and a blown-out yellow NPC lamp glow in the lower-left foreground is the brightest thing on screen. cavBuildEcho uses one PointLight (reach 46, decay 1.35) and a RingGeometry(0.86,1.0) floor ring. The chapter's premise is 'THE NOISE IS THE TORCH', but the noise shows the player very little.
findings.proposal: Keep the one light and add a wall answer. On each wheek, cast 24 rays in a horizontal fan against the cave walls using the existing collider/terrain query (cavTerrain or the wall list). For each ray, spawn a brief PALETTE.cavEcho glint (game.sparks with 3 particles, life 0.6) at the hit point, delayed by distance/20 s so the reveal travels outward and arrives back like a sonar ping. Thicken the ring to RingGeometry(0.7,1.0) and fade its opacity by radius. Cap the NPC lamp glow sprite's screen size near the camera. Flag it noEchoPing, costing about 24 sparks per wheek with a 1.05 s cooldown.

findings.title: [antarctic] The wake is stacked grey octagon rings like a line of tyres behind the boat
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-antarctic-03-pod-with.png and -04-end.png: behind the tender at speed there is a column of 8-10 identical grey octagonal rings, fully opaque at the stern, reading as washers or tyres rather than foam. The sea itself is one flat dark slab with no sheen, so the rings are the brightest thing in the lower half of the frame, during the chapter's marquee.
findings.proposal: In antBuildWake, replace the ring stack with two diverging V arms, a Kelvin wake: thin quads at +/-19.5 degrees from the stern, vertex-coloured white-to-transparent along their length, additive-free with Lambert opacity 0.35 fading to 0. Keep a short stern patch of white foam, three soft discs from the existing splash sprite. The arms' length scales with antBoatSpeed. Flag it noKelvin.

findings.title: [antarctic] The orca title and the calving countdown share the paper tab
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-antarctic-03-pod-with.png: while the pod is formed up on the boat, the one-line tab reads 'Drive the boat into the orca p... ▲13 m' with the subline 'the face goes in 45 s'. That subline is the 'the-calving' clue (systems.js:33195-33200), not the orca instruction ('W/S · A/D. find the blows, press Q, keep above 5.5 m/s', 33187-33191). In the marquee's own moment, the one line of instruction is about a different task 40 m to 400 m away.
findings.proposal: In the tab renderer, take the subline from the same task id as the title. If a live timer from another task wants the line, show it only when no wowLive is active. While the pod is escorting, prefer the orca clue's second form ('keep above 5.5 m/s with them'). Check that the recordLive/clue resolution for the tab uses the pinned task id.

findings.title: [drift] The live lantern count is worded as already done: 'lit it with 5 lampflies' shows before the lantern is lit
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3m-drift-04-plinth.png: standing at the unlit plinth with 5 of 6 flies, the tab subline reads 'lit it with 5 lampflies'. The E press refuses ('it wants light to start with. 5 of 6.'), and the lantern task is not done. drift.js:5005-5008 calls game.recordLive('lantern', driFliesAwake) while !driLit. The record row's label in shared.js:4962 is past tense ('lit it with'), so the live count tells the player the marquee has already happened.
findings.proposal: Add an optional liveLabel column to the record table ('lantern': liveLabel 'carrying'). Record rows are a static table, not save data, so no save field is added. Have the tab renderer use liveLabel when the value comes from recordLive, so it reads 'carrying 5 lampflies'. Audit the other rows (e.g. 'the-column', 'orca-ride') for the same tense problem.

findings.title: [cave] Lime-green cone ground cover and black-bar swiftlets break the Son Doong palette
findings.evidence: qa/ten-review/b3-cave-06-the-column.png and -07-wander.png, and b3m-cave-01-arr-a.png: the doline floor and the mouth are covered in saturated lime-green 6-sided pyramids that read as plastic spikes, the most saturated value in a chapter otherwise in mossy browns. b3m-cave-07-col-fall.png: the swiftlets that fly 'with you' in the drop are straight black bars like thrown sticks. The real doline is ferns and moss under a shaft of light.
findings.proposal: Swap the pyramid shoots for 2-3 crossed leaf blades (thin tilted boxes, the fern pattern the drift flora already uses), in a darker moss PALETTE entry, and lift the lightness only in the daylight pool using cavDaylightAt so green is brightest where the light falls. For swiftlets, use two swept-back wing triangles plus a body (crescent silhouette) and flap scale on the existing phase. Flag them noFern / noSwiftShape.

findings.title: [iceland] Reykjavik's streets are dim and empty, and the town does not lead to the hot pool
findings.evidence: b3-iceland run with real keys, following the minimap arrow from the pier toward the hot spring (-40,-10). The animal ended up against the side of a purple house at (17,115), 138 m out (qa/ten-review/b3-iceland-06-hot-spring.png). The minimap line goes straight through the house row, and nothing in the street (lamps, signs, people) points uphill. qa/ten-review/b3-iceland-02-list.png and -04-organ.png: the street is a wide grey-blue asphalt lane with parked box cars. The only warm light is window rectangles, and the church hill is a dark empty slope.
findings.proposal: Put a warm lantern trail up the one gap between iceROWS toward the geothermal field: 8 lamp posts (the existing street-lamp prefab with its road pool) spaced 12 m apart from the square to the spring. Add two locals walking that way with towels (existing crowd rig, a 'towel' prop box in PALETTE.iceSnow). Route the hot-spring hint through a waypoint at the gap, so the arrow follows the trail instead of the crow-fly line. The payoff is a visible warm path from town to the marquee.
